gotchas.procedure_section: Return - Schedule A (Medicare premiums from SSA-1099)
gotchas.title: Medicare Part B/D premiums in the SSA-1099 description
gotchas.trap: Ignore the Medicare premiums (and Linda's after-tax retiree premiums) when testing itemized deductions, or use net benefits ($35,718) as box 5.
gotchas.correct_treatment: Box 5 is gross $38,400 (premiums are included in benefits). Medicare B $2,220 + D $462 and the $3,960 after-tax retiree premium go to medical on the Schedule A comparison; after the 7.5% floor, itemized total still < standard deduction -> standard.

gotchas.title: Canadian pension in CAD
gotchas.trap: Enter CAD 24,000 as USD, omit it (thinking the treaty/Canadian tax covers it), or leave it out of the taxable SS computation.
gotchas.correct_treatment: Convert at the IRS 2025 yearly average (1.398): $17,167 on lines 5a/5b; it is included in provisional income for taxable SS (85% maximum reached).

gotchas.title: FTC on the Canadian pension: general category, no de minimis election
gotchas.trap: Claim the $2,575 directly on Schedule 3 without Form 1116, or classify as passive.
gotchas.correct_treatment: Pension is general-category income and not 'qualified passive income' reported on a payee statement, and $2,575 > $600 -> Form 1116 required. Limitation $1,183; credit $1,183; $1,392 added to the carryforward (total $3,860).

gotchas.title: RBC chequing account -> FBAR + Schedule B Part III
gotchas.trap: Answer Schedule B line 7a 'No' (the interest is tiny) and skip FBAR, or file Form 8938.
gotchas.correct_treatment: Max value CAD 37,912 = ~$27,653 (Treasury 12/31 rate) > $10,000 -> FinCEN 114 by Linda (due 4/15, auto-extended to 10/15); Schedule B Part III Yes / Canada; RBC interest is taxable. Form 8938 not required (below MFJ thresholds).

gotchas.title: Accrued interest paid at purchase
gotchas.trap: Report box 1 interest as shown ($2,431), or treat tax-exempt interest as taxable / omit it.
gotchas.correct_treatment: Subtract $386 'Accrued interest' on Schedule B (bond bought between coupon dates). Muni interest $3,115 on line 2a (not taxable, but counts in SS provisional income).

gotchas.title: Schwab IRA year-end statement in the PBC
gotchas.trap: Autoflow the IRA's dividends ($9,812), interest ($3,105) and gains ($14,280) onto Schedules B/D.
gotchas.correct_treatment: Income inside a traditional IRA is not reported; only distributions (1099-R) are taxable.

gotchas.procedure_section: Scan - Duplicate documents (corrected 1099-R) / QCD age test
gotchas.title: 'QCD' by a 67-year-old; corrected 1099-R
gotchas.trap: Use both 1099-Rs (double count $30,000) and/or exclude $8,000 as a QCD per the client and the original code Y.
gotchas.correct_treatment: Use the CORRECTED 1099-R only. A QCD requires the owner to be 70 1/2 on the distribution date (Robert: 11/14/2028). The full $30,000 is taxable (4b); the $8,000 is a cash charitable contribution usable only if itemizing (it isn't beneficial). No RMD was required (RMD age 73).

gotchas.procedure_section: Return - Schedule 1-A senior deduction / standard deduction age test
gotchas.title: Linda is 64 at 12/31/2025
gotchas.trap: Check both age-65 boxes (+$3,200) and claim the $6,000 senior deduction for both spouses (client says 'Linda is 65 this year').
gotchas.correct_treatment: Linda turns 65 on 03/22/2026 -> only Robert gets the $1,600 additional standard deduction and the $6,000 senior deduction (MAGI $115,341 < $150,000, no phase-out).

gotchas.title: Estimates + prior-year overpayment
gotchas.trap: Enter only the four $1,500 payments (or the organizer's $950 PY figure).
gotchas.correct_treatment: Line 26 = 4 x $1,500 + $1,150 2024 overpayment applied (per PY return) = $7,150.

assumptions: 1116 line 3 apportionment includes the Sch 1-A senior deduction with the standard deduction
Canadian employer pension non-contributory -> no US investment in the contract
QD/CG adjustment exception applies for Form 1116 (no foreign-source QD/CG)
